subject: BSM very slow, error messages appearing

messages.author: e6ac6506bddc9816
messages.subject: BSM very slow, error messages appearing
parts:
Hello,

I am running BSM after identifying the best fit model. In this case the model was BAYAREA+J and includes trait dependence. My tree is quite large (11,000+ tips) but my state space is small (10 ranges and 3 traits = 30 states). Model fitting only took about 8 hours.

I have two concerns. First, BSM is moving very very slowly. I ran it overnight and it is still on map 0 of 120. Second, each iteration gives me the same message:

Beginning stochastic mapping UPPASS (i:Leftnode,j:Rightnode,anc:Ancnode;):

22401:11204,22402:22207,anc:11203; Error in condprobs_Left_branch_bot %*% independent_likelihoods_on_each_branch[[i]] : 

  non-conformable arguments

Failure on stochastic mapping attempt #38/240 tries. Holding at success #0/120.

[1] "Error in condprobs_Left_branch_bot %*% independent_likelihoods_on_each_branch[[i]] : \n  non-conformable arguments\n"

attr(,"class")

[1] "try-error"

attr(,"condition")

<simpleError in condprobs_Left_branch_bot %*% independent_likelihoods_on_each_branch[[i]]: non-conformable arguments>


I have had success with BSM on the same size tree and state space with a DEC model and no traits (finished in a couple days) although the BAYAREA+J has the better fit. I am wondering what could possibly be causing the messages.

Thank you!

Liz

messages.author: 115d05260b0c341a
messages.subject: Re: [BioGeoBEARS] BSM very slow, error messages appearing
parts:
Hi -- unfortunately, BSM has not been programmed for trait-dependent dispersal models yet. It is theoretically possible, but would be a rather substantial project to do it as the BSM code would have to be refactored substantially.  

The "non-conformable arrays" means it is trying to multiply things of different sizes -- here, it is likely trying to multiply a 10x10 transition matrix by a 30x1 vector of probabilities. This will cause an error.

Normally a program would exit on these kinds of errors, but because BSM keeps trying to get a successful simulation, the program will keep trying until the number of tries is exhausted.

If you have a high need for this feature, email me off list and we can see if it is possible -- but I am on parental leave (just had baby #2) so it might take a bit.

Cheers,
Nick
